tasks.notes: Four core claims are fully supported, but core claim 1's 'single-digit millisecond averages' has no supporting quote — the supplied latency evidence says affected wide-partition reads fell from seconds to low double-digit milliseconds — so support is partial even though all five claims are addressed.
All five core claims are answered and supported by the supplied quotes on pre-commit log semantics, best-effort capture, lineage granularity, audit-record bindings and the required commit boundary.

All six core claims are answered and supported by the supplied quotes on capability expiry, metadata and capability scope, version and edge-copy retention, deletion inventory and separate access, retirement and deletion ownership.

Core claim 4's stale-snippet invalidation and exact-source fallback and core claim 5's late-authorization-filter risk are absent from both the answer and its quotes, so coverage and support are partial despite the otherwise strong BM25 analysis.

All six core claims are answered and supported by the supplied quotes on hop-local TLS, trusted forwarding, identity ambiguity, resource-side authorization, rotation and compromise separation, and negative tests.

Core claim 4 omits data size and skew, distributions and the user-count/'fast' rebuttal, and core claim 5 omits backup and restore, upgrades, staffing and failure drills, so both coverage and support are partial.

Core claim 2's 'components cannot be separated without untested side effects' fail condition and core claim 6's per-service rollback plan are absent from the answer and its evidence, making support partial despite broad seam, switch and removal coverage.

All five core claims are answered and supported: the answer exposes hidden weights and eliminated candidates, keeps constraints, evidence and outcome status separate, and treats pattern links as non-promotions.
All five core claims are answered and supported by the supplied quotes on equal-time outcomes, total ordering, declared priorities, the determinism-only test limit and stale-event handling.
